candidates.name: HM Land Registry plans: title plan (practice guide 40, supplement 5)
verified_facts: A title plan supports the property description in the register and provides a graphic representation identifying the general extent of land in a registered title.
The title plan must be viewed together with the register.
All title plans show general boundaries unless a boundary is shown as determined under section 60 of the Land Registration Act 2002.
Adjoining title plans can be based on different versions of Ordnance Survey mapping.
semantic_limits: A title plan, INSPIRE polygon or mapped red edging must not be promoted to an exact legal-boundary claim unless determined-boundary evidence exists.

candidates.name: HM Land Registry plans: boundaries (practice guide 40, supplement 3)
verified_facts: A legal boundary is an exact line but is rarely identified with precision on the ground or in conveyances/transfers and is not shown on Ordnance Survey mapping.
Physical boundary features may indicate only the general position of a legal boundary.
Registration with general boundaries leaves the exact boundary line undetermined unless a determined-boundary process applies.
semantic_limits: Parcel terrain QA may use published geometry for containment and repeatable sampling, but it cannot infer the exact legal boundary or ownership line from general-boundary mapping.
